articles.title: Man arrested after hidden camera found in San Jose Starbucks bathroom
articles.description: A San Jose man was arrested after a hidden camera was discovered in a public restroom at a Starbucks coffee shop last month, police said Thursday. The San Jose Police Department said an employee of the Starbucks on East Santa Clara Street in Downtown San Jose, just across the street from City Hall, discovered a camera under the sink in the restroom and reported it. Investigators checked the camera's footage and determined that it had been installed by an adult male suspect the same morning it was reported, police said. It had been up for about 30 minutes before it was discovered, and police found that it had recorded two victims, police spokesperson Stacie Shih. Using automated licence plate reader cameras, detectives with the department's sexual assault unit identified the suspect's car and the suspect, 38-year-old David Perales. On July 2, Perales was arrested in San Jose and booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail for invasion of privacy, police said. Anyone with information about this case or similar cases was asked to contact Detective Gregory #4435 of the Police Department's sexual assault unit at 4435@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-4102.

articles.title: San Jose: Man arrested for allegedly installing hidden camera in coffee shop bathroom
articles.description: SAN JOSE -- Police arrested a man arrested July 2 for allegedly installing a secret camera in the bathroom of a downtown coffee shop, authorities said. The 38-year-old man, a resident of San Jose, was booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of invasion of privacy, according to a news release Thursday from the San Jose Police Department. Around 9:30 a.m. June 9, an employee noticed a hidden camera in the public restroom of the coffee shop, which is located on the 100 block of East Santa Clara Street, and reported it to police, authorities said. SJPD's Sexual Assaults Investigation Unit carried out an investigation which found that the camera was installed by an adult man earlier that morning and identified the suspect with the assistance of SJPD's Real Time Intelligence Center and Automatic License Plate Reader cameras, authorities said. Police then obtained an arrest warrant for the suspect, authorities added. Anyone with further information on this incident is asked to contact Detective Gregory #4435 at 4435@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-4102.

pendingReview.title: Wilsonville man sentenced for bathroom hidden camera
pendingReview.description: PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) - A Wilsonville man was sentenced on Thursday after secretly filming a mother and her teen daughter in his home bathroom, according to court documents. Marcelino Mauro Vera-Ramirez, 44, was sentenced to six months in jail and must register as a sex offender. The sentence comes as Vera-Ramirez, a licensed chiropractor with an office in Tigard, pleaded guilty to invasion of privacy charges in February. According to the Clackamas County District Attorney's Office, a woman and her 14-year-old daughter were staying in his home. In June 2024, the DA's Office said the girl had stepped out of the shower when she noticed a camera in a waste basket attached to a cellphone that was "camouflaged with toilet paper." The girl then told her mother who found the camera had been removed, authorities said. The following month, the mother got out of the shower and saw the hidden camera in the waste basket. Both took the camera to Wilsonville police, who obtained a search warrant, finding multiple videos of the mother and daughter "nude or partially nude," the DA's Office said, noting they also found video of Vera Ramirez setting up the hidden camera. Vera Ramirez was taken into custody in December 2024, and he pleaded guilty to four counts of invasion of privacy on Feb. 17.
